items.title: Randy Brecker interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 12, 2022
items.q: I had listened to him as a kid... I heard James Brown... for the first time and that had a — you know I probably sat up straight in bed. That just hit a nerve.

ctx.x: Well during those times that was kind of bashing — jam sessions, a lot of free music, Coltrane was everyone’s idol, and high intensity and playing was the hors d’oeuvres so to speak of the day. So in the early 60s that all sunk in I suppose and of course when Mike discovered Coltrane that was it for him. And I was in the throes, when I first moved to New York, of the Brecker-Liebman-Bob Berg-Steve Grossman complex where they played together quite a bit. And I was in on that so I was around a lot of tenor players,…
Would that include James Brown? © Fillius Jazz Archive -8-

Oh sure, sure. I had listened to him as a kid you know, going back to when I was still home in Philly the R&B station — it’s unusual — most guys will say that they listened to rock & roll or R&B first and then they caught on to jazz. I did the opposite. I hadn’t heard all this other stuff, I was just hearing bebop at home.
